name: IDS Evaluation Framework
description: The growing number of security threats on the Internet and computer networks demands highly reliable security solutions. Meanwhile, Intrusion Detection (IDSs) and Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPSs) have an important role in the design and development of a robust network infrastructure that can defend computer networks by detecting and blocking a variety of attacks. Reliable benchmark datasets are critical to test and evaluate the performance of a detection system. There exist a number of such datasets, for example, DARPA98, KDD99, ISC2012, and ADFA13 that have been used by the researchers to evaluate the performance of their intrusion detection and prevention approaches. However, not enough research has focused on the evaluation and assessment of the datasets themselves. In this paper we present a comprehensive evaluation of the existing datasets using our proposed criteria, and propose an evaluation framework for IDS and IPS datasets.
evaluation_method: Dataset quality criteria combined with downstream IDS performance metrics such as detection rate (recall), false positive rate, F1 score and AUC
general_score_metric: F1 (detection) and false positive rate for downstream IDS evaluations; qualitative dataset-quality scores for the framework itself
notes: Framework paper rather than a single dataset benchmark; cautions that many IDS datasets (e.g., KDD99, DARPA98) are outdated, synthetic, or suffer class imbalance, redundancy and contamination risk—limits external validity for modern traffic.
